slice: the explaining: a genome is an artifact of prior living

items.section: 1.3 Every self is a same-existing-society of selves
items.text: A genome is an artifact of prior living, a non-living stable form a living cell goes on with: a cell transcribes it, re-forms it and passes it on, and each doing a field gives a genome or a sequence, entering, copying, hiding, is a living cell's, as Natural Medicine's own saying seats each verb of agency at a cell.

items.section: 5.3 Fourteen rungs at fourteen primes, and the fold at twenty-four
items.text: Seventeen's gene closes as a self in its pattern-matching and re-forming, and the genome it re-forms from is an artifact of prior living, a non-living stable form; the rung's self is that living re-forming, and the sequence is its artifact.

A genome is an artifact of prior living, as 2.4 says of each prior in stable form: a field's genome that copies, an element that moves, a virus that enters, each gives an artifact a doing that is a living cell's going on with it.
